objectives.description: Add v7 entry to batch-admit-schema.md Version History

approaches_tried.approach: Searched docs/architecture/orchestrate-state-machine.md exhaustively for an admission-dimension/defer_reason enumeration to update (grep for 'admission layer', 'admission dimension', quoted defer_reason literals, 'fifth'/'fourth'/'sixth')
approaches_tried.reason: this file is an overall state-machine stage/move description, not an admission-gate reference doc; its one incidental self_modifying/file_scope_collision mention (line ~1311, deferred_self_modifying field description) is already accurate prose unaffected by the new dimension, and its one 'not a fifth admission gate' sentence (line ~1317) is about deploy_checkpoint NOT being counted among orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's dimensions at all -- a different axis, also unaffected. The plan's Phase 6 Scope Hypothesis anticipated this file might need an update; on inspection it genuinely does not, same pattern as Phase 2's and Phase 4's recorded design findings

scope_hypothesis_confirmation.note: file-footprint-overlap.md was NOT found by this grep at all (it discusses the Overlap/Containment predicate, not defer_reason/absent_file_scope literal text) but IS one of the plan's explicitly-named Files-to-modify, handled on its own merits per its own named task. The 4 extra files beyond the hypothesized set (multi-task-operations.md, orchestrate-batch-results-template.md, task-lock.md, state-management-schema.md, multi-task-creation-standard.md -- 5 actually, since orchestrate-state-machine.md and batch-admit-schema.md were already in the hypothesized 4) were each individually inspected: every one uses file_scope_collision/absent_file_scope as a ONE-OFF illustrative example or a narrower domain-specific enumeration (e.g. multi-task-operations.md's bounded-second-pass tier list, which already omits absent_file_scope and is unaffected since whole_tree_claim correctly falls under its existing 'every other defer flavor' catch-all), never an authoritative admission-dimension/defer_reason catalog requiring a whole_tree_claim addition. None were edited.
scope_hypothesis_confirmation.a_fifth_file_in_scope: docs/architecture/orchestrate-state-machine.md (one of the originally-hypothesized 4) was inspected but found to contain no actual enumeration -- see approaches_tried above.

important_code_fix_during_documentation_.summary: While tracing docs/architecture/batch-admit-schema.md's Version History (which documents that every prior defer_reason bump added a matching case arm to orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's closed case statement in the SAME change), discovered Phase 4 had NOT added a whole_tree_claim case arm there (Phase 4's own Files-to-modify list was orchestrate-batch-admit.sh only). Without it, every whole_tree_claim defer would silently fall into the loud default/unrecognized arm -- excluded from dispatch (correct practical effect) but recorded into unrecognized_defer_reason_ledger with a scary WARNING instead of a clean defer_ledger entry. Fixed: added a whole_tree_claim) case arm to orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh mirroring file_scope_collision's shape, plus a new Group 34b regression test. Recorded via issue-record.sh (class coverage-gap, severity costly).

verification.suite_result: both green -- cycle-plan: 384/0 (up from 382/0 after adding Group 34b's 4 new assertions), batch-admit: 15/0 (unaffected by documentation edits)

The pre-existing, unrelated patterns/task-lock.md mismatch (sibling task's concurrent edit) was deliberately left untouched again, same as Phase 5 -- see that phase's unrelated_drift_note. Remaining [core] FAILs are all 'deployed script content drift', the expected Phase-3/4/5/6 source-store staleness Phase 7 resolves.
